facts.text: Simulation credibility must be scaled to the risk of a wrong decision and is conditional on intended use.
facts.quote: Credibility must be scaled to the risk of a wrong decision, and it is conditional on intended use.

facts.text: A defensible simulation safety claim specifies the model version, inputs, decision and domain for which sufficient evidence exists; saying only that a simulator is validated is incomplete.
facts.quote: "This simulator is validated" is an incomplete safety statement; the defensible claim is "version X of this model, using these inputs, has sufficient evidence for decision Y inside domain Z".

facts.text: Verification and validation are different activities.
facts.quote: Verification and validation are different activities

facts.text: Calibration against a test does not demonstrate predictive capability on independent data; the FAA states this explicitly, and ASME, NASA and NRC make the same separation.
facts.quote: calibration against a test is not demonstration of predictive capability on independent data. The FAA states this explicitly; ASME, NASA and NRC make the same separation.

facts.text: Model validation must use independent physical data from inside the intended envelope.
facts.quote: Validation must be against independent physical data from inside the intended envelope.

facts.text: Model-to-model comparison can help debugging but is not accepted as validation.
facts.quote: Model-to-model comparison can help debugging but is not accepted as validation.

facts.text: Simulation credibility deteriorates fastest during extrapolation, which needs an explicit margin; Columbia provides a stark demonstration.
facts.quote: Extrapolation is where credibility deteriorates fastest, and it needs an explicit margin. Columbia is the stark demonstration

facts.text: The FAA limits simulation use to conditions similar to those used for validation.
facts.quote: the FAA limits use to conditions similar to the validation.

facts.text: Simulation reports to decision makers must include uncertainty and caveats.
facts.quote: Reports to decision makers must carry uncertainty and caveats

facts.text: No single scalar score represents simulation credibility.
facts.quote: no single scalar score represents credibility.

facts.text: No universal percentage of physical tests that must remain was found, and claims that a particular percentage is inherently sufficient are unsupported.
facts.quote: no universal percentage of remaining physical tests was found. Mature frameworks decide the allocation from model influence, decision consequence, applicability and uncertainty; claims that a particular percentage is inherently sufficient are not supported.

facts.text: Mature simulation frameworks allocate physical testing according to model influence, decision consequence, applicability and uncertainty.
facts.quote: Mature frameworks decide the allocation from model influence, decision consequence, applicability and uncertainty

facts.text: Some physical confirmation remains in every regulator-level simulation scheme found.
facts.quote: Some physical confirmation always remains in every regulator-level scheme found.

facts.text: On-road evidence shows threshold effects in degraded visibility, including fog in chamber tests and darkness in AAA tests.
facts.quote: Field results show threshold effects in degraded visibility: fog in the chamber tests, darkness in the AAA tests.
